presentingComplaint: Progressive breathlessness, palpitations and a near-collapse while mobilising on post-operative day 4.
history: Admitted 5 days ago after a fall with a displaced intracapsular fractured neck of the right femur, treated with a cemented hemiarthroplasty on day 1. Estimated intra-operative blood loss was moderate and a post-operative wound drain filled twice. Over the last 48 hours he has become increasingly fatigued, breathless on minimal exertion and reports pounding palpitations; today he felt light-headed and nearly collapsed when the physiotherapist stood him up. He has passed two loose black tarry stools. Background of permanent atrial fibrillation, ischaemic heart disease with a prior NSTEMI, hypertension and osteoarthritis. Polypharmacy on admission: apixaban 5 mg BD, aspirin 75 mg (inadvertently continued alongside the anticoagulant), bisoprolol, amlodipine, atorvastatin, furosemide and long-term omeprazole; he was also given regular ibuprofen for post-operative analgesia. No overt haematemesis. No prior known anaemia; last documented Hb 6 months ago was 12.8 g/dL.
examination: Elderly man, visibly pale with pale conjunctivae and palmar creases, cool peripheries and prolonged capillary refill. Comfortable at rest but breathless on speaking. Chest clear with no crackles; JVP not raised. Heart sounds normal, irregularly irregular pulse, soft ejection systolic flow murmur. Abdomen soft and non-tender; rectal examination reveals melaena. Surgical wound clean and dry with no surrounding erythema or discharge. No focal neurology.
imaging: Erect chest radiograph: no consolidation, effusion or pulmonary oedema; heart size normal. Post-operative pelvis film: well-sited cemented right hemiarthroplasty.
microbiology: Not indicated; no clinical features of infection. Blood cultures not sent.
differentialDiagnoses: Symptomatic anaemia from acute-on-chronic blood loss (peri-operative loss plus upper GI bleeding on dual antithrombotics/NSAID)
Upper GI (peptic ulcer) haemorrhage as the underlying source
finalDiagnosis: Symptomatic anaemia (Hb 6.8 g/dL) due to acute-on-chronic blood loss in a peri-operative elderly patient on dual antithrombotic therapy plus an NSAID, with clinical decompensation (exertional dyspnoea, palpitations, presyncope, demand tachycardia).
citations: AABB Red Blood Cell Transfusion Thresholds and Storage Guidelines 2023
BSH Guideline on the Investigation and Management of Iron Deficiency and Iron Deficiency Anaemia 2021
stewardship: Non-infective presentation; no antimicrobial therapy indicated. Management focus is haemodynamic stabilisation and correcting the anaemia and its cause: stop the aspirin and NSAID and hold/reverse the apixaban, high-dose IV proton-pump inhibitor and urgent upper GI endoscopy for the suspected bleeding source. Transfuse red cells using a restrictive threshold (Hb <7 g/dL, or <8 g/dL given his cardiovascular disease and active symptoms) targeting Hb 7-9 g/dL, transfusing single units with reassessment between units to avoid TACO in an elderly cardiac patient on furosemide. Investigate and treat iron deficiency (low ferritin/transferrin saturation) with iron replacement once bleeding is controlled. Antimicrobial stewardship not applicable.
contraindications: Avoid liberal/over-transfusion and rapid multi-unit transfusion given age, cardiac disease and diuretic use (TACO risk)
Do not continue aspirin plus NSAID alongside a DOAC in an actively bleeding patient
Avoid oral iron as sole strategy while GI bleeding is uncontrolled
edgeCases: Microcytosis and low ferritin/transferrin saturation confirm co-existent iron deficiency, but ferritin can be falsely elevated by post-operative inflammation and should be interpreted with transferrin saturation
Raised urea with normal-range creatinine supports an upper GI source rather than pure peri-operative loss
Symptomatic threshold, not an absolute Hb number, drives urgency; demand tachycardia and presyncope indicate physiological decompensation
expectedMaiK: Symptomatic anaemia is defined by tissue hypoperfusion and cardiorespiratory compensation (dyspnoea, palpitations, presyncope, tachycardia), not by an absolute haemoglobin value; identify and stop the bleeding source, use a restrictive transfusion threshold (raised to <8 g/dL in cardiovascular disease) and correct underlying iron deficiency.
expectedNextQuestions: Any haematemesis, coffee-ground vomiting or change in stool colour/frequency?
Exact current drug list including anticoagulant, antiplatelet and NSAID doses and last doses taken?
Estimated intra-operative and drain blood loss and trend of serial post-operative haemoglobins?
Any chest pain, orthopnoea or leg swelling to distinguish cardiac decompensation from anaemia alone?
expectedInvestigations: Serial full blood count with haemoglobin trend
Iron studies (ferritin, transferrin saturation), B12 and folate
Coagulation screen and anti-Xa/apixaban level if available
12-lead ECG and troponin to assess demand ischaemia

investigations: Serial full blood count and haemoglobin trend
